system_map.overview: The repository pairs a Python CAS runner with LLM clients, governance engines, steering fact models and agent-facing documentation. A central runner orchestrates execution, while typed governance, compliance and steering structures provide constraints, evaluation and traceability.

patterns.name: Pluggable LLM Provider Client

tool_protocols.notes: No MCP or explicit tool-call schema was visible in the supplied evidence.

optimisation_targets.notes: A stable client boundary reduces provider-specific integration risk and supports deterministic substitutes.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: The client boundary limits provider-specific autonomous behaviour and keeps model access explicit.

patterns.summary: LLM access is isolated into concrete client classes so CAS code can call models through a stable interface.
patterns.intent: Hide provider-specific model invocation and allow deterministic substitutes for local or tested flows.
patterns.context: src/cas_runner/llm provides LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient, while pyproject.toml depends on litellm.
forces: model provider APIs differ across vendors
agent flows need reproducible execution without network instability
governance logic should not embed provider details
patterns.solution: The runner or downstream components use a client class rather than litellm directly; LiteLLMClient wraps the real provider and MockLLMClient supplies controlled outputs.
implementation_signals: separate llm package with concrete client classes

evidence.note: Concrete client wraps litellm for model access.
Alternative client enables controlled LLM responses.

costs: client abstraction must cover all required provider capabilities
failure_modes: mock client diverges from real provider behaviour
client becomes a restrictive anti-pattern if too narrow

patterns.reuse_notes: Introduce a small LLM client protocol whenever agent flows need provider abstraction and deterministic substitutes.

patterns.name: Centralised Flow Runner Pipeline

tool_protocols.notes: Tool protocol usage inside FlowRunner is not visible from the supplied symbols.

optimisation_targets.notes: A single runner gives predictable ordering and a central place for stop or retry logic.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Execution is centralised for control, while agents may still perform model-based decisions inside steps.

patterns.summary: A central FlowRunner appears to coordinate multi-step CAS flow execution from the CLI.
patterns.intent: Give flows a single, inspectable execution point instead of scattered ad hoc agent invocations.
patterns.context: src/cas_runner/runner.py contains FlowRunner and src/cas_runner/cli.py contains main; documentation describes orchestration and automated run flows.
forces: flows need predictable ordering
execution must be inspectable for governance
CLI entry points need a common execution path
patterns.solution: CLI code invokes or routes to FlowRunner, which appears to coordinate flow execution. Documentation names orchestration and automated run flow as first-class architecture concerns.
implementation_signals: CLI main entry point in cli.py
docs referencing orchestration flow and automated run flow

evidence.note: Central runner class for flow execution.
CLI entry point that likely invokes flow execution.
Documentation indicates a defined execution sequence.

benefits: single control point for flow execution
costs: runner can become a bus factor or bottleneck
unknown stop conditions if code body is not inspected
failure_modes: steps may rely on undocumented mutable context
failure isolation may be weak if runner swallows errors

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a central runner class for multi-step agent flows when execution order, tracing and governance need to be explicit.

patterns.name: Typed Governance State Contracts

tool_protocols.notes: Typed data models are the visible interface rather than a tool protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Typed state makes governance data harder to corrupt and easier to validate.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Contracts restrict agent or engine freedom to emit arbitrary governance state.

patterns.summary: Pydantic models define governance inventories, health, risks, actions, findings and metrics.
patterns.intent: Make governance state explicit, validation-friendly and portable between engines and dashboards.
patterns.context: src/cas_runner/governance/models.py defines multiple governance and compliance models, supported by pydantic and jsonschema dependencies.
forces: governance engines need shared vocabulary
compliance findings must be auditable
health and metrics must be comparable across runs
patterns.solution: Use typed models such as GovernanceInventory, GovernanceHealth, GovernanceRisks, ComplianceFinding, ComplianceMetrics, GovernanceAction and ResolutionResult as the shared governance contract.
implementation_signals: many governance domain models in one module
metric and finding models co-located with action models

evidence.note: Defines governance and compliance state objects.
pydantic and jsonschema dependencies support typed contracts.

costs: schema changes may require coordinated updates
failure_modes: models drift from runtime reality
overly strict validation blocks useful partial state

patterns.reuse_notes: Define explicit typed contracts whenever multiple components must reason about governance, compliance or agent-produced state.

patterns.name: Transition-Registry Governance Action Engine

tool_protocols.notes: The visible mechanism is registry-backed action resolution, not external tool calls.

optimisation_targets.notes: A transition registry constrains autonomous state changes to known paths.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Autonomy is bounded by an explicit registry of allowed transitions.

patterns.summary: GovernanceActionEngine and TransitionRegistry manage explicit governance state transitions and actions.
patterns.intent: Prevent arbitrary governance state changes by resolving actions through known transitions.
patterns.context: src/cas_runner/governance contains GovernanceActionEngine, TransitionRegistry and GovernanceActionService, while models define GovernanceAction and ResolutionResult.
forces: governance state changes must be auditable
autonomous engines should not invent transitions
service layer must present a stable action API
patterns.solution: A transition registry defines allowed transitions; GovernanceActionEngine resolves state and emits GovernanceAction objects; GovernanceActionService exposes the action workflow.

evidence.note: Engine and registry indicate bounded state transitions.
Models define action and resolution payloads.

benefits: clear separation between transition policy and action execution
failure_modes: registry misses valid transitions
engine silently resolves to weak default actions

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a transition registry when agent or engine state changes must be constrained to known governance paths.

patterns.name: Compliance Evaluation Guardrail

tool_protocols.notes: Compliance appears to consume typed governance state rather than external tools.

optimisation_targets.notes: Findings and metrics provide a measurable guardrail around agent or governance behaviour.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Evaluation state is structured into findings and metrics rather than open-ended advice.

patterns.summary: ComplianceEngine converts governance state into findings, risks and metrics to support safe decisions.
patterns.intent: Make governance and agent activity measurable against compliance rules before further action is taken.
patterns.context: src/cas_runner/governance contains ComplianceEngine and compliance-oriented models such as ComplianceFinding, ComplianceMetrics and GovernanceRisks.
forces: agent actions need measurable safety checks
risk must be visible before propagation
findings must be usable by dashboards or action engines
patterns.solution: ComplianceEngine evaluates typed governance state and emits ComplianceFinding and ComplianceMetrics objects, with GovernanceRisks representing risk state.

evidence.note: Models define compliance output and risk state.

costs: false positives may block useful work
failure_modes: rules cover only narrow cases
metrics drift from actual risk

patterns.reuse_notes: Add a dedicated compliance evaluator when agent or workflow outputs need structured findings and metrics before promotion.

patterns.name: Explainable Governance Health Model

tool_protocols.notes: Health calculation appears to consume governance state rather than call tools.

optimisation_targets.notes: Reason strings help humans and agents understand status without deep inspection.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Health is a derived, explainable status rather than autonomous decision.

patterns.summary: The dashboard health model calculates status and reasons from governance state.
patterns.intent: Make system or governance health inspectable and explainable to operators or downstream agents.
patterns.context: src/cas_runner/dashboard/health_model.py defines HealthStatus, calculate_health and get_health_reasons, alongside GovernanceHealth in governance models.
forces: operators need quick status understanding
governance state may be complex
status must be explainable, not opaque
patterns.solution: calculate_health produces a HealthStatus from governance inputs, and get_health_reasons produces human-readable reasons for that status.

evidence.note: Governance health is modelled as typed state.

costs: reason strings must stay aligned with metrics
failure_modes: health status becomes a stale label
reasons are too vague to act on

patterns.reuse_notes: Pair status scoring with reason generation whenever agent system health must be surfaced to humans or other agents.

patterns.name: Evidence-Derived Steering Facts

tool_protocols.notes: Steering may consume repository and prompt evidence through future extractors, but no extractor symbols were supplied.

optimisation_targets.notes: Deriving steering from facts and lineage reduces reliance on unsupported model claims.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents may steer freely, but the steering model requires typed evidence and lineage.

patterns.summary: Steering models turn raw git deltas and prompt facts into typed capability records, lineage and architectural deltas.
patterns.intent: Make architectural steering traceable to repository and prompt evidence rather than unexplained generation.
patterns.context: src/cas_runner/steering/models.py defines GitChangeType, RawGitDelta, PromptFact, SteeringRuntimeIndex, CapabilityCategory, CapabilityRecordType, CapabilityRecord, CapabilitySet, CapabilityLineage and ArchitecturalDelta.
forces: steering decisions need traceability
git changes and prompt outputs are heterogeneous evidence
capability growth needs lineage over time
patterns.solution: Raw git deltas and prompt facts are modelled as evidence; capability records and sets encode derived capability state; CapabilityLineage and ArchitecturalDelta preserve trace and change impact.

evidence.note: Models for evidence-derived steering and capability lineage.

costs: fact extraction and normalization are required
failure_modes: fact extraction misses important signals
lineage becomes stale or disconnected

patterns.reuse_notes: Use typed evidence facts plus lineage whenever agent steering decisions must be tied to repository, prompt or operational traces.

patterns.name: Bootstrap Governed Agent Workspace

tool_protocols.notes: Workspace bootstrap is file/document-oriented in the supplied evidence.

optimisation_targets.notes: Pre-provisioning governance reduces repeated instruction drift across agents.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents inherit prepared constraints instead of discovering them at runtime.

patterns.summary: Bootstrap initializes a workspace and merges a CAS governance block into agent-facing context.
patterns.intent: Ensure agents start with a governed, initialized workspace rather than relying on runtime prompt assembly.
patterns.context: src/cas_runner/bootstrap.py defines merge_cas_governance_block, bootstrap and init_workspace, while agent instruction files exist at the repository root.
forces: agents need consistent initial constraints
workspace setup should be repeatable
governance text should be injected rather than repeated manually
patterns.solution: init_workspace prepares the workspace, bootstrap coordinates initialization, and merge_cas_governance_block appears to merge governance blocks into agent-facing materials.

evidence.note: Functions indicate workspace preparation and governance block merging.

benefits: governance text managed in one merge point
costs: bootstrap logic must be maintained with governance docs
failure_modes: governance block merges into the wrong target
bootstrap leaves a partially initialized workspace

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a bootstrap step when agents require prepared workspaces, injected governance blocks or consistent prompt context.

patterns.name: Multi-Agent Instruction Manifests

tool_protocols.notes: Skill directories suggest tool or CLI integration, but no protocol code was supplied.

optimisation_targets.notes: Separate manifests allow each agent ecosystem to use familiar instruction formats.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents have tool-specific manifests but share repository-level governance documents.

patterns.summary: The repository provides separate instruction manifests and skill directories for different AI agent ecosystems.
patterns.intent: Support multiple coding-agent tools while preserving shared repository governance and skills.
patterns.context: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md exist at the repository root, with .agents/skills/hf-cli and .claude/skills/hf-cli directories.
forces: different agent CLIs expect different configuration files
repository policies should remain shared
skills need portable discovery locations
patterns.solution: Provide agent-specific instruction manifests alongside shared architecture and governance docs, and place reusable skills under agent-specific skill directories.

benefits: tool-specific instructions without duplicating all policies
failure_modes: agent-specific file overrides shared governance unintentionally
skills are available only to one agent ecosystem

patterns.reuse_notes: Maintain a general agent manifest plus tool-specific manifests and skill directories when supporting multiple coding-agent systems.

patterns.name: Structural CI/CD Policy Validation

tool_protocols.notes: Validation is procedural against workflow files, not an agent tool protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Policy checks constrain automated runs before they execute.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Workflow behaviour is constrained by explicit structural checks.

patterns.summary: A workflow validator enforces structural invariants on CI workflows, including hardcoding, pinned installers, dry-run reachability and retired workflows.
patterns.intent: Prevent brittle or inconsistent automated workflows before they can affect agent-facing continuous execution.
patterns.context: specs/090-simplify-cicd-workflows/validate_workflows.py contains several check functions and a main entry point.
forces: CI workflows are execution surfaces for agents or automated systems
hardcoding and unpinned installers cause drift
retired workflows and unreachable dry-run paths create ambiguity
patterns.solution: validate_workflows.py checks YAML syntax, zero hardcoding, unpinned installer usage, unreachable dry-run paths, retired workflows, trigger remediations and composite action adoption.

evidence.note: Validation workflow exists for CAS builds.

benefits: makes CI policy visible and testable
costs: validators must be maintained as workflows evolve
policy changes may require migration work
failure_modes: check logic does not cover new workflow idioms
validators pass but semantic workflow risk remains

patterns.reuse_notes: Use structural validators for any agent-facing CI where workflow files are executable contracts.

patterns.name: Template-Driven Pattern Evolution and Promotion

tool_protocols.notes: The pattern is document- and template-oriented rather than tool-protocol oriented.

optimisation_targets.notes: Templates make pattern evolution deliberate and reviewable.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents or humans may propose artifacts, but template stages structure the lifecycle.

patterns.summary: Templates and documentation define a lifecycle for signals, heuristics, patterns, experiments, learnings and promotion decisions.
patterns.intent: Keep architectural learning durable by moving evidence through controlled artifact states.
patterns.context: cas-knowledge/templates contains templates for patterns, heuristics, signals, rules, learnings, experiments, promotion decisions and architecture records; docs include pattern evolution flow.
forces: ad hoc notes do not scale
patterns need promotion criteria
agents and humans must share the same artifact shape
patterns.solution: Use templates to create consistent artifacts and use governance docs or promotion decisions to move items from signal or heuristic to pattern or rule.

evidence.note: Template for promoting heuristics to patterns.

benefits: clear promotion path from observation to pattern
failure_modes: templates are created but not maintained
promotion decisions become formality without evidence

patterns.reuse_notes: Use template-driven promotion when an agent system must accumulate reusable architectural knowledge over time.

patterns.name: Runtime Execution Context Store

optimisation_targets.notes: Persistent runtime context supports audit, resume and evaluation.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: The pattern is inferred from directory structure rather than runtime control flow.

patterns.summary: A runtime directory stores execution profile, rule context, evaluations and traces as persistent run context.
patterns.intent: Keep run-specific context, rules, evaluations and traces outside source code so flows can be inspected or resumed.
patterns.context: cas-knowledge/runtime contains execution-profile.yaml, rule-context.json, evaluations and traces.
forces: runs need audit artifacts
rule context may vary by project or environment
evaluations and traces should not be lost with process state
patterns.solution: Store execution profile and rule context as machine-readable files, and keep evaluations and traces as runtime artifacts.

evidence.note: Execution profile stored as runtime configuration.
Rule context stored as runtime JSON.

benefits: separation of code and run state
costs: storage and cleanup policy is needed
failure_modes: context files are written but never read
traces grow without retention

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a dedicated runtime artifact directory when agent flows need profiles, rule contexts, traces or evaluations that outlive a process.

patterns.name: Agentic Merger Artifact Reconciliation

tool_protocols.notes: The symbol name suggests merging, but the supplied evidence does not show tool protocol usage.

optimisation_targets.notes: A merger can reconcile agent-produced governance artifacts with canonical state.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: The concrete autonomy of the merger cannot be verified from symbol evidence alone.

patterns.summary: AgenticMerger appears to reconcile or merge agent-produced governance artifacts.
patterns.intent: Combine agent-generated or modified governance artifacts into a consistent state without silent corruption.
forces: agents may produce overlapping governance artifacts
merged state must remain traceable
governance models require consistent vocabulary
patterns.solution: An AgenticMerger class appears to be the dedicated component for merging governance-related agent output, likely using governance models as the target contract.

evidence.note: Dedicated merger class for agent-produced governance artifacts.

costs: merge semantics must be explicitly defined
failure_modes: merger silently drops valid agent changes
merge result violates later validation

patterns.reuse_notes: Use a dedicated merger when multiple agents or engines emit artifacts that must be combined into canonical governance state.

anti_patterns.name: Hardcoded Values in CI/Agent Workflows
symptoms: Workflow logic embeds fixed values instead of externalized configuration
Automated runs bypass governed configuration sources

anti_patterns.name: Unpinned Installer Invocations
symptoms: Automated workflows install tools or packages without pinned versions
Execution can change between runs due to external package updates
suggested_remediation: use a composite action or cached build environment

anti_patterns.name: Retired Workflow Lingering
symptoms: Deprecated workflows remain present and potentially discoverable
Operators or agents may trigger the wrong execution surface
